---
title: "Small multiples that move"
description: "A faceted animation: facet_wrap() and transition_time() together, one panel per continent, every panel on the same frozen scales, each bubble kept inside its own panel."
categories: [Animation]
image: figs/animated-facets-poster.png
---



[The gapminder bubble chart](gapminder.qmd) puts every country in one panel, coloured by
continent. Splitting it into small multiples makes each continent's path easier to
follow, and it takes one more line: `facet_wrap()` composes with `transition_time()`
like any other layer of the grammar.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(gapminder)

g4 <- transform(gapminder[gapminder$continent != "Oceania", ], pop = pop / 1e6)
g4$continent <- droplevels(g4$continent)

a <- vplot(g4, width = 7, height = 4.5) |>
  mark_point(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp, size = pop, color = continent,
             data_id = country, alpha = 0.7) |>
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10", breaks = c(1e3, 1e4, 1e5),
                     labels = c("1k", "10k", "100k")) |>
  facet_wrap(~continent) |>
  guides(color = "none") |>
  labs(title = "Year: {round(frame_time)}", x = "GDP per capita",
       y = "Life expectancy", size = "population (millions)") |>
  transition_time(year) |>
  animate(nframes = 100, fps = 20)
```
:::



::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](figs/animated-facets.svg){width=100%}
:::
:::


Oceania's two countries are left out to keep the grid at two by two, and
`droplevels()` drops its now-empty level so it gets no panel.

## What faceting changes

- **Every panel in every frame.** The panels come from the whole data, so the grid is
  fixed for the length of the animation. A year in which a continent had no rows would
  leave its panel empty rather than removing it.
- **Identity includes the panel.** A bubble is matched by `data_id = country` *within*
  its panel, so it never slides from one panel into another. Here each country stays in
  its continent; in data where a row's facet value changes between states, the mark
  fades out of one panel and into the other.
- **Shared, frozen scales.** The scales are trained once over all years and all panels,
  so the panels can be compared with each other and with themselves over time. Free
  scales (`facet_wrap(scales = "free")`) would have to retrain per frame and are
  refused for an animation.

The output is an animated SVG of about 3.4 MB, around 350 KB compressed on the wire.
